body_markdown:
The battle for supremacy in the pickup market is perhaps America’s most fiercely contested automotive arena. The diesel heavy-duty battle, in particular, has reached stratospheric heights in the past decade: Four-figure torque specs, mid-five-figure towing capacities, and six-figure price tags are shockingly common. Now, General Motors looks like it’s raising the bar even higher with the announcement of a new 8.3-liter version of the Duramax turbodiesel engine. Make way for the “Mongoose.”


The announcement came via a 37-second film that gives off a nature documentary-meets-cage match vibe. A Mongoose appears, with pupils that go from round to bowtie-shaped. It battles a scorpion in the shade of a bush with a GMC logo growing out of it. Not exactly your typical context for pitching a heavy-duty truck, but it works, we suppose. (By the way, did you catch what pattern the scorpion was walking in? The shape of an oval! As we said—this Detroit-area rivalry is in full swing.)


Since its introduction in 2001, every iteration of the Duramax turbodiesel V-8 (six or seven generations thus far, depending on how you slice it) has displaced 6.6 liters. Smaller Duramax engines exist, like the[3.0-liter straight-six for light-duty pickups](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-chevrolet-silverado-1500-zr2-review-diesel-power/) and[full-size GM SUVs](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-chevrolet-suburban-review-staying-fresh-90-years-later/) , and an even smaller 2.8-liter four-cylinder Duramax for the[mid-size Colorado](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/review-2022-chevrolet-colorado-zr2-bison/) and Canyon, but the Mongoose marks the first time a consumer-grade Duramax will go even bigger.


The Mongoose joins two new[next-generation V-8s](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/report-gms-new-small-block-v-8-due-in-dual-displacements/) slated for use in GM light-duty pickups. Displacing 5.7 and 6.6 liters, the new small-block V-8s are slated to debut in the[2027 Chevy Silverado 1500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-chevrolet-silverado-specs-pictures/) and the GMC Sierra 1500, both of which are due by the end of this year.


GM hasn’t released any power figures for the Mongoose yet, but keep in mind that the current-generation L5P produces 470 hp and 975 lb-ft of torque. You can bet your boots that the Mongoose will crack the four-figure torque mark.
